human_tolerance.notes: The Japanese article records it nesting in trees, on old nests and on buildings, and feeding on the ground in gardens and parks; it is a common resident of Japanese suburbs.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeds almost year round in warm parts of the range, with a flimsy platform nest and two eggs; northern populations move south in winter.

vocalizations.description: The male's characteristic four-note cooing song, traditionally rendered in Japanese as 'de-de poppo'; given mainly at dawn from a perch.
Soft cooing contact note between a pair.
Sharp, clipped alarm note given on take-off.

taxonomy.note: The GBIF species match on Streptopelia orientalis returns usageKey 2495681, rank SPECIES, status ACCEPTED, order Columbiformes, family Columbidae, genus Streptopelia, authorship (Latham, 1790).

external.note: gbif_usage_key 2495681 from the GBIF species match; inat_taxon_id 2927 from the iNaturalist taxa API (active, rank species, preferred common name 'Oriental Turtle-Dove'); wikidata Q704987 from the English Wikipedia page's wikibase item.

range.note: The article gives a wide native range from Central Asia east across Asia to Japan, with subspecies covering central Siberia to Japan and Korea south to the Himalayas, the Ryukyu Islands, Taiwan, southern India and from Orissa and Bengal to Myanmar and Hainan. The country list is a derivation from that prose; resident Japanese birds are the nominate S. o. orientalis.

traits.note: Mass 232.94 g is the EltonTraits BirdFuncDat BodyMass-Value for Streptopelia orientalis. Length about 33 cm is the Japanese article's figure; the English article says it is a little larger than the European turtle dove and about the size of a collared dove without giving a number. Locomotion Walk and Fly: the article says it is 'predominantly granivorous and forages on the ground'. Diet follows EltonTraits (seed 40, fruit 20, plant-other 40) with the plant-other share folded into seed and a small insect share added from the Japanese article, giving seed 0.7, fruit 0.2, invertebrate 0.1. Lifespan 5 years is carried from the congener mourning dove record and is a judgement. Wingspan_m 0.58 is the midpoint of the German Wikipedia's 54-62 cm Flügelspannweite for the species.

habitat.note: The Japanese article records it nesting in trees, reusing old nests and sometimes on buildings, and feeding on the ground in gardens and parks; use ground 0.6 / arboreal 0.4, shelter on a perch, and resources follow the granivorous ground diet and the flimsy platform nest.

seasonal.note: The Japanese article records breeding almost year round with two eggs, an incubation of 15-16 days and fledging about 15 days later; northern populations migrate south in winter while Japanese birds are largely resident, so strategy ActiveYearRound. Juvenile duration 31 days is the sum of the sourced incubation and fledging periods.

vocalizations.note: The Japanese article describes the male's song, traditionally rendered 'dē-dē poppo', sung mainly at dawn, and a general food and habitat account; the contact and alarm calls are a judgement for a dove. The three calls map onto the program's song, contact and alarm slots.

look.note: The English article describes a dove with a black-and-white striped neck patch, a browner scaly wing than the turtle dove and a wedge-shaped tail; the Japanese article adds the blue-and-white neck bars and a red bare eye-ring. The modelled neck patch carries the blue neck bar; proportions and palette are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: food_tag seed follows the granivorous ground diet, song and alarm bind the cooing song and the take-off alarm, and nest months bracket the long breeding season.
